hints: Look closely at what is different about the lagging strand, it is made in short separate pieces rather than one continuous strand.
Remember what the word ligase suggests, to ligate means to join or link, so ask which box describes joining pieces together.
walkthrough:
**Recall what happens on the lagging strand**

Think of the lagging strand as being built in short bursts. Because DNA polymerase can only work in the $5'$ to $3'$ direction, this strand is made as separate Okazaki fragments.

Key idea: separate fragments must later be joined into one continuous strand.

**Match each enzyme to its job**

Helicase unwinds the double helix in stage A. Single-stranded binding proteins keep strands exposed in stage B. DNA polymerase synthesises the new fragments in stage C.

Key idea: DNA ligase has one special job, to seal the gaps and form phosphodiester bonds between fragments.

**Pick the linking stage**

Only stage D says the fragments of newly formed DNA are linked together. That description is exactly the job of DNA ligase.

Conclusion: D is the ligase stage.

options.A: This unwinding step uses DNA helicase to break hydrogen bonds, not DNA ligase.
options.B: This exposing step is stabilised by single-stranded binding proteins, not by ligase.
options.C: This synthesis step uses DNA polymerase to add nucleotides in the 5' to 3' direction, not ligase.
options.D: This is correct because DNA ligase joins Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand by catalysing phosphodiester bond formation.
